concept.name: Partial fill
concept.definition: An execution of only part of an order's quantity, leaving the remainder open (or canceled, depending on the order's time-in-force). Partial fills occur whenever available contra-side liquidity at acceptable prices is smaller than the order.
concept.intuition: You asked for 1,000, the market gave you 300 - the rest is still working unless the order says otherwise.
concept.mechanics: Venues report the executed portion with cumulative and remaining quantities; in FIX the order state becomes Partially Filled with CumQty < OrderQty and LeavesQty > 0, and the invariant OrderQty = CumQty + LeavesQty holds while the order is active. IOC orders cancel the remainder immediately; FOK orders never partially fill by construction.
concept.formula: LeavesQty = OrderQty - CumQty (FIX quantity invariant for an active order).
concept.failure_modes: Partial fills leave sub-scale positions that distort strategy economics (fixed fees spread over fewer shares) and can strand a hedged pair half-executed. In fast markets, repeated small partials also accumulate impact without achieving the intended size.
concept.misconceptions: A partially filled order is not done - unless its time-in-force says otherwise, the balance keeps working and can still execute. Nor can an FOK order partial-fill; 'partial' presumes the order type permits it.
concept.example: Your limit order to buy 1,000 shares at $25 catches only 400 before the offer lifts; the execution report shows CumQty 400, LeavesQty 600, and the 600-share balance keeps working at $25.

citations.source: FIX 4.2 Execution Report (MsgType 8), FIX Dictionary (Onix Solutions)
citations.section: OrdStatus = Partially Filled; OrderQty = CumQty + LeavesQty
